summary: Initial discovery focused on where to host embeddings and rerank: hosted vs dedicated vs private. Customer concerned about tail latency at 10k qps, vector DB integration, embedding dimensionality (768 vs 1536), fallbacks for high load, and security (VPC, KMS). Redwood outlined caching, batching, and quantized model options; agreed to run a throughput smoke test and share pricing + security docs.
topics: vector DB integration and hybrid search
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Carlos and Tess from our engineering team.
[00:12] Lena Park: Hi, Lena from InnateAnalytics. We're trying to figure out where to run embeddings and rerank. we've got traffic spikes and need consistent tail latency.
[00:22] Rahul Mehta: Hi, Rahul here. interested in throughput numbers, especially at higher qps and how fallback to cheaper variants works.
[00:30] Carlos Ruiz: Great. quick clarifying question, what's your current vector DB? are you on a managed store or self-hosted?

[00:38] Tom Briggs: We're on a mix — primary store is a managed cluster (we call it VectorX) but we also keep hot shards in Redis for low-latency stuff. exploring moving more to a vector-first setup but cost is a concern.
[00:50] Tess O'Neil: ok thanks, that helps. and approximate qps and topk? like 1k steady 10k peaks, topk=10?

[01:00] Sofia Alvarez: yes roughly 1k steady and spikes to 8-12k during business hours. topk mostly 5-10. embedding dims are currently 1536 for best quality, but we're open to experimenting with 768 hybrids.

[01:15] Maya Chen: perfect — so main tradeoffs are cost vs latency vs quality. Redwood Hosted can get you started fast, Dedicated gives predictable throughput, and Private/VPC for strict compliance and network control. we'll dig into each.
[01:28] Lena Park: can you be specific on latency at scale? like 250ms p95 for rerank is our target, ideally lower.

[01:36] Carlos Ruiz: yes. with dedicated pools we tune batch sizes, KV cache, and kernel selection so p95 for a 1536-dim rerank with topk 10 is often in the 120-200ms range depending on batching and GPU type. hosted is similar but with multi-tenant variability — we offer SLAs on Dedicated.
[01:55] Rahul Mehta: multi-tenant variability sounds risky. do you have mitigations? we've seen noisy neighbors wreck tail latency.

[02:03] Carlos Ruiz: good point. mitigation is twofold: isolated CUDA contexts on Dedicated, and across-host routing + fast fallback models. we also do prefix KV caching, so repeated prefixes don't re-compute kv. plus auto-burst to extra capacity if configured.
[02:20] Tom Briggs: what about model quantization — can we run 8-bit to save cost and what's the accuracy delta?

[02:26] Tess O'Neil: quantization works well for many of the candidate models; for rerank you generally see small drops in MRR, maybe 1-3% depending on dataset. we can run evals on your sample prompts to measure precisely.
[02:40] Lena Park: ok. and vector DB integration — we want to keep VectorX for storage. how do you recommend integrating? proxied queries? hybrid rerank?

[02:48] Carlos Ruiz: typical pattern: vector store handles ANN search for candidate recall, then Redwood does a rerank call where we call the model with the topk vectors + context. you can also use a hybrid flow where lexical filters run first then vector fanout. Redwood supports streaming and tooling to pass IDs and embeddings to your DB.
[03:05] Rahul Mehta: latency budget for two-hop: if vector DB returns topk in 30ms, how much does rerank add?

[03:11] Carlos Ruiz: depends on batch size; single-item rerank with a small prompt is ~60-120ms on Dedicated for 1536-dim when optimized. if you batch multiple reranks we can amortize overhead. also, we expose routing to place rerank in the same AZ to avoid network hop.
[03:26] Sofia Alvarez: networking — we need VPC peering and KMS integration. can Redwood support customer-managed KMS keys and HSM?
[03:33] Maya Chen: yes, Private and Dedicated both support KMS integrations. Private can use customer HSM. we'll share our KMS integration guide. also support SSO/SAML and RBAC for console access.
[03:44] Lena Park: perfect. SOC2 attestation? log retention? we need audit logs for model queries (at least meta, not payloads).
[03:51] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC2 Type II. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. we keep token-level usage metrics; payload retention is configurable per contract in Private.
[04:00] Tom Briggs: back to dims — 1536 gives us slightly better relevance for long-tail queries. but if 768 with rerank is close, that's a big cost saver. thoughts?

[04:08] Tess O'Neil: in our benchmarks we've seen 1536 provide marginal gains mainly on rare queries; a hybrid approach is common — use compact embeddings for recall, then full-precision for rerank when needed. also sharded vectors and topk=50 recall then rerank top10 works well.
[04:24] Rahul Mehta: how do you handle sharding and fallback if a node is overloaded?

[04:29] Carlos Ruiz: routing policy: either allow fanout to more shards (costly) or degrade to fewer-rank passes with caching. Redwood has automatic fallback to a smaller model or cached rerank results based on policy thresholds.
[04:40] Lena Park: examples of fallback policy?

[04:43] Carlos Ruiz: e.g., if p95 latency > 300ms, route new requests to a quantized model with a cached rerank estimate; if that still fails, degrade gracefully to lexical-only results with a note — we can set those thresholds per route.
[04:58] Tom Briggs: what's the runbook for the throughput test you mentioned?

[05:02] Carlos Ruiz: we'll need a representative query set, your vector DB can run recall latencies in parallel and return topk. Redwood will spin up a dedicated pool matching target GPU spec, run fanout+rerank at 10k qps for short interval to surface tail latency and error rates. we'll coordinate time and VPC/network settings.
[05:20] Lena Park: we can provide a 20k query sample and a staging VectorX cluster. who will own the infra for the test?
[05:25] Maya Chen: Redwood will provision test capacity in Dedicated and coordinate network peering; you'll provide sample data and test harness credentials. Carlos will draft the plan.
[05:34] Rahul Mehta: cost modeling — can you show cost per 1M reranks by config?

[05:38] Maya Chen: yes we'll send a breakdown: hosted vs dedicated vs private; dedicated shows lower per-token cost but involves commitment. we'll put an example using 1536 vs 768 dims and also factor in vector store cost for recall.
[05:49] Sofia Alvarez: security question: does Redwood ever store raw PII in logs? we need to avoid that by default.
[05:55] Tess O'Neil: by default we mask or avoid storing request payloads unless configured. Private deployments can be configured to never persist payloads and only keep telemetry.
[06:05] Tom Briggs: any known limits on KV cache size or TTL?
[06:09] Carlos Ruiz: depends on cluster size; cache can be tens to hundreds of GB, TTL configurable. we often keep a hot prefix cache for minutes to hours depending on traffic patterns.
[06:18] Lena Park: what's the expected onboarding timeline for Private?
[06:21] Maya Chen: Private typically 8-12 weeks for on-prem; VPC-hosted Private is 4-6 weeks with faster network config. Dedicated can be provisioned in days once contract is signed.
[06:31] Rahul Mehta: do you support model version pinning and can we rollback to a previous model on failover?
[06:36] Tess O'Neil: yes, rollout policies allow canary, A/B, and instant rollback. you can pin routes to fixed model versions for consistency.
[06:45] Tom Briggs: curious about developer ergonomics — SDKs, observability?

[06:49] Maya Chen: we have SDKs in Python/Node/Go, observability includes per-route latency/cost breakdown, token-level tracing, and custom metrics. we'll demo Console if you want a walkthrough next week.
[07:02] Lena Park: that'd be useful. can we also see a sample rerank trace so we understand token cost?
[07:06] Carlos Ruiz: absolutely — we'll include a sample trace in the follow-up and annotate the cost per step.
[07:12] Rahul Mehta: one more Q — hybrid search: do you recommend scoring composition (lexical+vector) or rerank only?

[07:18] Tess O'Neil: both valid. scoring composition (linear interpolate) is cheaper when vector distances are reliable. rerank gives better QA but costs more. many customers do hybrid recall + rerank for best of both.

[07:30] Lena Park: ok great. i want to call out our success criteria: p95 rerank <250ms at 10k qps, MRR lift >8% vs lexical baseline, and SOC2-compliant logging. if we can hit those, we'll pilot dedicated.

[07:44] Maya Chen: clear. we'll treat that as the acceptance criteria for the pilot. next steps: we share pricing and security docs, Carlos drafts the smoke-test plan, schedule the test, and reconvene after results.
[07:56] Tom Briggs: timeline for pricing/plan?
[07:59] Maya Chen: pricing in 3 business days; Carlos plan in 2 business days. are there any other stakeholders we should include?
[08:05] Sofia Alvarez: yes include our networking/security lead (Marcus Lee). I'll share contact info via email.
[08:10] Maya Chen: thanks Sofia. we'll send calendar invites for a demo + test kick-off. any final quick questions?
[08:16] Lena Park: not from me. appreciate the practical guidance — the fallback policies sound promising.
[08:21] Rahul Mehta: sounds good. excited to see the throughput numbers.
[08:24] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and test plan. end call.
[08:30] [call ended]
